Resting Monday. Gordon (rest) will miss Monday's preseason matchup against Phoenix, Harrison Wind of TheDNVR.com reports. The high-flying forward will miss his first preseason contest. Gordon's next chance to suit up comes Wednesday against the Clippers.

A little bit of everything in loss. Horford amassed 13 points (3-8 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in 29 minutes during Friday's 137-134 preseason loss to the Raptors. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

May not be ready for opener. Nesmith could be sidelined for the start of the regular season due to a foot injury, Scott Agness of FieldhouseFiles.com reports. A first-round pick in 2020, Nesmith saw a rotational role on the wing for Boston through his first two NBA seasons before being included in the Malcolm Brogdon trade this offseason. The 22-year-old is expected to handle a similar assignment this season for Indiana, but once healthy he could see more minutes for the Pacers than he did for the Celtics.

Getting locked in for third year. Sengun is expected to have the third-year option on his rookie contract picked up, Jonathan Feigen of the Houston Chronicle reports. The young center earned his spot in the Rockets' future plans with a solid rookie season that saw Sengun average 9.6 points and 5.5 rebounds over 72 games as a teenager. Houston will likely keep all four of its 2021 first-round picks in the fold for the 2023-24 campaign, with Jalen Green, Josh Christopher and Usman Garuba all expected to have their options picked up.

Logs 14 minutes off bench. Drummond amassed six points (2-2 FG, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block in 14 minutes during Friday's preseason victory over the Nuggets. Drummond figures to slot in as the primary backup behind Nikola Vucevic, a role that inspires little confidence when it comes to fantasy value. While he can accumulate boards and defensive stats in limited minutes, there is no reason to draft him outside of deeper formats only.

Fourth-year option picked up. Pokusevski's fourth-year rookie option was picked up by the Thunder on Saturday. The 17th overall pick from the 2020 Draft out of Serbia, Pokusevski is still in the midst of proving his full potential. He saw a reduction in role last season and averaged 7.6 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 20.2 minutes. It's possible he sees an uptick this season, but the Thunder have no shortage of development options all vying for court time.

Removed from starting lineup. Pokusevski will not start in Tuesday's preseason matchup with the Pistons, Keith Langlois of the Pistons' official site reports. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Undecided on potential return. Iguodala has an open invitation to rejoin the Warriors but has yet to decide whether or not to retire, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports. Iguodala could fill the Warriors' 14th roster spot if he decides to return. Next season would be his 19th in the league, and he is coming off a championship with Golden State.

Could have roster spot next season. The Warriors will save a roster spot for Iguodala in case he decides to continue playing next season, according to Anthony Slater of The Athletic. The Warriors only have 11 players on standard contracts so far and have at least three openings on their projected regular-season roster, and it's possible one of those spots will be filled by Iguodala if he wants to play for another season. Golden State hasn't set any sort of deadline for Iguodala to make a decision on whether or not he wants to continue his playing career, so there will be a roster spot available for him if he decides he wants to continue playing.

Nabs two steals in win. Caruso finished with 11 points (4-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three steals, two assists and one block in 15 minutes during Friday's 131-113 preseason victory. Despite the injury to Lonzo Ball, Caruso's role could remain largely unchanged when the season opens. His recent injury history, as well as the addition of Goran Dragic, means the Bulls can afford to manage him in the hope of a more robust season. Even in limited minutes, Caruso has the ability to be an elite source of steals, making him a viable late-round target in competitive drafts.

Expected to begin season as starter. Caruso is expected to open the 2022-23 season as the Bulls' starring point guard, speculates Darnell Mayberry of The Athletic. Caruso probably makes the most sense as Lonzo Ball's short-term replacement given his experience, leadership and defensive abilities. He's not the best offensive player out of the group of contenders for the starting point guard role, but the Bulls do not really need him to fill that role if he's playing alongside Zach LaVine, DeMar DeRozan and Nikola Vucevic.

10 points in win. Wiggins compiled 10 points (4-9 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-3 FT), a rebound and three assists in 16 minutes of a 104-95 preseason win Sunday over Washington in Japan. Wiggins has looked a bit rusty in the first two preseason games, going 2-for-9 from behind the arc. He's played 16 minutes in both contests and combined to score 15 points. The 27-year-old made his first All-Star team last season -- averaging 17.2 points and 4.5 rebounds in 73 games -- and looks to repeat that performance as the Golden State aims to defend its title.

Pistons might chase him. The Pistons might make a move for Wiggins in free agency next year, according to Marlowe Alter of The Detroit Free Press. The Pistons could open up to nearly $69 million in cap room next summer if they want to make a significant impact in the 2023 free agent market, and Wiggins is believed to be one of the players they might target. He would be an excellent fit for Detroit as a scoring threat to pair with young players such as Cade Cunningham and Saddiq Bey, but it remains to be seen if he tests the open market or if he decided to sign an extension with the Warriors before next summer.

Option exercised for 2023-24. The Timberwolves exercised the $13.53 million option for Edwards in 2023-24 on Saturday. Edwards has been everything he was billed to be coming out of the 2020 NBA Draft, compiling 21.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.5 steals over 34.3 minutes per game last season. He will serve in a starring role in the backcourt again, but there will also be another mouth to feed down low following the team's offseason acquisition of All-Star Rudy Gobert.

Cleared for training camp. Simons (knee) will be available for training camp, Danny Marang of BlazersEdge.com reports. Simons had a breakout campaign last season as Damian Lillard struggled through injuries, but both point guards were eventually shut down for the remainder of the campaign. Across his final 27 appearances last year, Simons posted 23.4 points, 5.8 assists and 2.7 rebounds with shooting splits of 46/42/87. He inked a four-year, $100 million contract this offseason and figures to garner a major role next to Lillard in Portland's backcourt.

Locks down starting job. Bulls coach Billy Donovan said Dosunmu will be the Bulls' starting point guard to begin the season, Rob Schaefer of NBC Sports Chicago reports. Dosunmu has been starting for the Bulls in the preseason with Lonzo Ball (knee) out. Ball is expected to be out at least a few months, but will likely return this season. Until he returns, the second-year guard should be in line for a breakout season. As a rookie, Dosunmu averaged 8.8 points, 3.3 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 0.8 steals in 27.4 minutes across 77 games. Donovan having confidence in a second-year player over veterans such as Goran Dragic, Alex Caruso and Coby white speaks to the potential the young guard has.
Set to start in preseason opener. The Bulls announced that Dosunmu would start versus the Pelicans on Tuesday. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Hands out 10 assists in win. Simmons produced seven points (3-5 FG, 1-4 FT), 10 assists, eight rebounds and two steals over 28 minutes in Wednesday's preseason victory against Milwaukee. Simmons' performance was right in line with what we've come to expect from him -- he struggled from the free-throw line and took a backseat as a scorer but put up big numbers as a rebounder and passer, leading the team with 10 assists and finishing second with eight rebounds. Through three exhibition contests, the Australian guard is averaging 5.7 points, 7.3 boards, 6.3 dimes and 1.3 steals across 24.3 minutes. In fantasy leagues, his ability to put up numbers across multiple categories is balanced by a complete absence of three-point shooting and a poor percentage from the charity stripe.

Nash won't pressure PG to shoot. Nets head coach Steve Nash said Wednesday that he doesn't care if Simmons "ever shoots a jump shot," Nick Friedell of ESPN.com reports. After the Nets' second full training camp practice, Nash said that Simmons is "very unique." The coach believes that the 6-foot-11 point guard's versatility makes him special, not his shooting, so Nash wants Simmons to stick to what makes him comfortable. The most important thing for Simmons, who missed the 2021-22 campaign, is his health. He's been a full participant to start training camp and shouldn't have any limitations heading into the 2022-23 campaign.

Mathurin hit all four of his shots in the first quarter, the last two of which came off assists from Andrew Nembhard. The Pacers guard was quiet after that until the fourth quarter when he added another nine points on 3-of-5 shooting. However, he also fouled out of the game (albeit with 24 seconds left), with five of his fouls coming in the fourth.

Scores 22, grabs 6 boards. Adebayo scored 22 points (9-17 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT) with six rebounds, two assists and two steals in 25 minutes against the Timberwolves on Wednesday. It wasn't the best start for Adebayo as he shot just 2-of-7 from the field with two turnovers in the first quarter. That changed when the Heat's big man entered the game for Haywood Highsmith in the second quarter and collected four rebounds - two offensive - while adding six points on 3-of-4 shooting. Adebayo would knock down seven of his last 10 shots in the game before sitting out for the fourth quarter.

Not on table in Durant deal. Adebayo is not a player the Heat are interested in trading away as part of any Kevin Durant deal, Barry Jackson and Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports. Miami's reluctance to include the 25-year-old All-Star in a deal may have taken it out of the running for Durant, although Brooklyn doesn't appear close to making a trade with any other club. Even if the Heat were willing to include Adebayo, the Nets couldn't acquire him without also shipping out Ben Simmons due to the Designated Rookie Extension rule, making such a deal even more unlikely.

Inks one-year deal with Boston. The Celtics signed Griffin to a one-year contract Friday, Adrian Wojnarowski of ESPN reports. The Celtics signed Danilo Gallinari this offseason to fortify their frontcourt depth, but he tore the ACL in his left knee while playing for the Italian national team in EuroBasket 2022 in late August, likely ending his 2022-23 campaign before it began. Boston also is expected to be without Robert Williams, who's set to miss the first couple months of the season following arthroscopic surgery on his left knee, so Griffin figures to slide into a reserve role behind Al Horford and Grant Williams. Griffin will compete with Luke Kornet and Sam Hauser for reserve minutes, but both of those players are floor-stretches, so look for Griffin to serve as the top defensive big man off Boston's bench to start the season.

Scores 15 points in loss Saturdday. Portis closed with 15 points (7-14 FG, 1-4 3Pt) and five rebounds in 20 minutes during Saturday's 118-109 loss to the Hawks. Portis did his thing on the offensive end as the Bucks opted to go with a different look. While he is slated to come off the bench behind Brook Lopez, Portis still has the ability to put up fantasy-worthy numbers even in limited minutes. His value is tied to points and rebounds which does cap his overall upside. With that being said, he remains an option for managers in need of a cheap center late in drafts.

Traded to Pistons. Bogdanovic was traded to the Pistons from the Jazz on Thursday in exchange for Kelly Olynyk and Saben Lee, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports. After dealing two franchise centerpieces in Donovan Mitchell and Rudy Gobert, the wheels were in motion for the Jazz to continue selling off veteran assets, so Bogdanovic being on the move doesn't come as much of a surprise. Utah will bring back much-needed help at center in Olynyk, while Lee is a young player who could earn minutes on what will be a rebuilding Jazz team in 2022-23. Bogdanovic, whose contract expires after this coming season, could push for a starting spot in Detroit -- either at shooting guard or small forward. For the Pistons, the decision will likely come down to whether they prioritize immediate results or the development of young players like Saddiq Bey and No. 5 overall pick Jaden Ivey.

Could be on Phoenix's radar. Bogdanovic could be a target of the Suns in a trade, Brian Windhorst of ESPN reports. Phoenix has been engaged in active trade talks over the last week involving the expiring contract of Jae Crowder, among other players, and Bogdanovic is someone who could be a fit coming back the other way. The 33-year-old also has only one year remaining on his current deal and has averaged at least 18 points and two made three-pointers a game in each of the last four seasons.

Making progress in recovery. Bogdanovic is making progress in his recovery from a knee injury but is not expected to be available for Opening Night, Lauren L. Williams of MLive.com reports. The fact that Bogdanovic is not expected to play in the season opener shouldn't be surprising, as recovery from surgery is always a bit tricky. The Hawks want the him to be at full strength before he returns to the court, and they have plenty of backcourt depth to mitigate Bogdanovic's absence. The sharpshooter has spent the last two seasons with Atlanta, averaging 15.1 points per game across 107 regular-season contests.

Drops game-high 24 points in loss. Hyland totaled 24 points (7-14 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 6-7 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one block in 22 minutes during Friday's loss to the Bulls. Hyland continues to push for more playing time, impressing with a polished offensive performance. The lack of peripheral numbers remains a question mark, although based on what we saw to close last season, he certainly warrants being drafted in the later rounds of just about every draft.

Productive minutes Thursday. Clarke amassed 16 points (5-8 FG, 6-7 FT), five rebounds, two assists, a steal and a block in 18 minutes in Thursday's 126-111 victory in Detroit. Clarke lived in the paint in his 18 minutes, grabbing five offensive rebounds and never attempting a shot beyond four feet. It was his best scoring night of the preseason and second time he reached double-digits. He's averaging 19.0 minutes and 10.2 points on 54.2 percent shooting and 14-for-17 from the charity stripe.

No rust to shake off. Ingram finished with 19 points (7-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-5 FT), one rebound, three assists and one steal over 20 minutes in Friday's preseason game against the Hawks. Ingram didn't miss a beat in his preseason debut, shooting efficiently from the field while also distributing the basketball. He missed the last few exhibitions due to a toe injury but will be at full strength entering the regular-season opener Wednesday in Brooklyn.

Not on table in Durant deal. Ingram is not a player the Pelicans are willing to trade, even in a deal for Kevin Durant, Christian Clark of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports. Instead, New Orleans wants to give its young nucleus a chance to grow together, and Clark notes that Ingram and Zion Williamson have only been on the floor together for 81 games since they were paired up in 2019. Ingram has averaged better than 22 points per game in each of his three seasons with the Pelicans after being acquired from the Lakers in the Anthony Davis deal.

Joins Minnesota. Forbes and the Timberwolves agreed to a contract Friday, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports. Forbes helps make up for some depth lost in the Wolves' trade to acquire Rudy Gobert. Over the past two seasons, Forbes has shot 43.4 percent from three on 4.4 attempts per game. It's possible he sees a marginal increase in role compared to his time in Denver last season, where he saw 17.1 minutes per game.

Taking night off Tuesday. Lopez will not play in Tuesday's game against the Bulls, Chuck Swirsky of the Bulls Radio Network reports. Barring an additional report to the contrary, it's pretty safe to assume the veteran big man is just getting a breather in this one. Lopez and Bobby Portis remain the primary tandem down low for the Bucks entering the 2022-23 campaign, with Lopez hopefully slated for a larger contribution this season after dressing for just 13 contests in 2021-22 due to injury. Milwaukee notably has back-to-back preseason contests to close it out, so Lopez could be back in action as soon as Wednesday.

Not expected to sign extension. The Bucks are not expected to give Lopez a contract extension before the start of the 2022-23 season, according to Eric Nehm of The Athletic. The veteran big man is entering the final year of his contract. While he remains a key piece for Milwaukee, the team will probably determine the fate of several players, including Lopez, depending on what happens with the franchise and their title aspirations. Lopez is slated to earn $13.9 million in 2022-23.

Shines on defense. Hield scored seven points (3-8 FG, 1-4 3 Pt) with five rebounds, two assists and three steals across 20 minutes in Wednesday's win over the Hornets. Hield scored five of his seven points in the first half on 3-of-8 shooting, but it was on the defensive end where he really made his presence felt. The Pacers guard collected three rebounds in the first quarter and grabbed three steals in the second, two of which came off of bad passes from LaMelo Ball. Hield would later be replaced by Bennedict Mathurin early in the third quarter and would not return as the Pacers continue to give extra rest to their starters before the regular season kicks off.

Key figure in active trade talks. Per Adrian Wojnarowski via ESPN, The Lakers and Pacers are engaged in "on and off again" talks discussing a deal centered around Hield, Myles Turner, Russell Westbrook and draft capital. Hield and Turner would represent major upgrades for Los Angeles, but the franchises are at an impasse, as the Lakers are currently "not willing to give up" two future first-round picks for Indiana's package. Reportedly offering one first-round pick previously, it's very possible an extended stalemate ensues.

Won't return Tuesday. Reddish won't return to Tuesday's preseason game against the Pistons due to a sprained left ankle. The Knicks won't risk anything here, as Reddish apparently tweaked his ankle sometime during Tuesday's preseason matchup. Reddish finished with three points, one rebound, one assist and one block in 11 minutes before exiting. It's unclear at the moment if he'll be able to participate in the team's next game Friday against Indiana.

Content with Knicks?. Reddish did not request a trade this offseason, per Fred Katz of The Athletic. On Sept. 1, Marc Berman of the New York Post relayed that Reddish "wants a change of scenery." Although the vernacular is different, Kats seemingly refutes that. Reddish averaged 6.1 points, 1.4 rebounds and 0.8 steals in 15 games for the Knicks last season while only logging 20-plus minutes twice. He's currently slated for a similarly small bench role on a deep Knicks squad.
Hoping for trade. Reddish prefers a trade due to a lack of playing time on the Knicks, Marc Berman of the New York Post reports. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Won't play Thursday. Martin has been ruled out for Thursday's preseason game against the Nets due to a knee issue, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Martin started Tuesday's preseason opener against the Timberwolves and totaled 12 points, three rebounds, two assists and one block in 22 minutes of action. He'll remain on the sidelines for Miami's second preseason game as he tends to the knee injury, so his next chance to return will be for Friday's exhibition against the Grizzlies.

Should see more minutes at PF. Martin will likely see more usage in the frontcourt this season following the departures of P.J. Tucker and Markieff Morris from the Heat, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports. As a restricted free agent, Martin signed a three-year deal to remain in Miami that was worth less than a potential offer sheet he would have gotten from another club had he waited. In return, the 26-year-old's loyalty will probably be rewarded with more court time, and he intends to bulk up this offseason in order to better handle the physical requirements of bumping under the basket with larger opponents. "I think that's part of being versatile, is me being able to do something like that," Martin said Tuesday. "You could sit here and say that I'm not a four or a wing or whatever, but I think I'm a basketball player and I adjust to any position."
Returning to Heat. Martin signed a three-year, $20.5 million contract with the Heat on Wednesday, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Set to start in preseason opener. LeVert will start at small forward in Wednesday's preseason opener versus Philadelphia, Chris Fedor of Cleveland.com reports. Cavaliers coach J.B. Bickerstaff has yet to iron out the starting small forward for the regular season. Isaac Okoro, LeVert, Cedi Osman, Dylan Windler, and Dean Wade will all be competing for the spot. LeVert will get a good chance to earn that role Wednesday night. Last season he averaged 17.0 points, 4.3 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 30.7 minutes across 58 games for both the Cavaliers and Pacers.

Bench role likely?. LeVert could be viewed as a sixth man after the acquisition of Donovan Mitchell, per Chris Fedor of Cleveland.com. LeVert, with his "ball-dominant, score-first, attacking play style, seems like a logical sixth man candidate," opines Fedor. The 28-year-old split time as a starter and sixth man last season, averaging 13.6 points, 3.9 assists and 3.4 rebounds in 19 games with Cleveland.

In talks on extension. Johnson is in talks with the Suns about a rookie scale extension, Brian Windhorst of ESPN reports. The deadline for reaching a deal on an extension is Oct. 17, and if the Suns can't get Johnson signed, he will become a restricted free agent next offseason. The 26-year-old's production took a big step forward in his third NBA season in 2021-22, and speculation earlier this summer suggested his extension could be worth more than $15 million per year.

Struggles in preseason loss Monday. Osman scored just four points (1-7 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT) in 17 minutes during Monday's preseason loss to the 76ers. Osman was barely visible in the loss, doing very little to convince the coaching staff that he should be handed a significant role this season. While the team is yet to decide on who will start as the small forward, Osman appears as though he will not be given the job. Barring injuries to other players, he is not worth drafting outside of deeper formats only.

Mentioned again in trade rumors. Osman's name has come up in recent trade rumors involving Jae Crowder, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. The Cavaliers were mentioned as a suitor for almost every big-name player available via trade this summer until they finally landed Donovan Mitchell. While Osman's name was usually involved, he didn't end up being part of the package sent to the Jazz. Cleveland could still be looking to trade for a starter at small forward, and Osman is the most logical candidate to trade places with Crowder. However, the team's proximity to the luxury tax threshold may not make a deal for the veteran forward feasible. As the Cavs' roster currently stands, Osman is one of the main competitors for that open starting spot, along with Caris LeVert and others.

Might miss opener. Boucher won't play in Friday's final preseason game due to a hamstring injury and may not be ready for the Raptors' season opener October 19 against the Cavaliers, Lori Ewing of The Toronto Star reports. Otto Porter is also dealing with a hamstring issue that could sideline him for Toronto's opener, potentially leaving the frontcourt short-handed behind starters Pascal Siakam and Scottie Barnes. Boucher saw his numbers take a step backward last season, but he played a career-high 80 games while averaging 9.4 points and 6.2 rebounds in 21.1 minutes a night.

Bench role forthcoming. Wood will operate as a sixth man to open the season, relays Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com. Wood is reportedly "motivated to finally have a chance to win in the NBA and not too worried about whether he starts or comes off the bench." Puts up 11 points in loss. Rozier registered 11 points (4-13 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three assists, two steals and a rebound across 25 minutes in Sunday's 134-93 loss to the Celtics. Rozier has never been known for shooting at an elite clip, but his role as one of the team's go-to players on offense shouldn't be questioned as the regular season approaches.

Likely to come off bench this year. Hardaway (foot) is expected to come off the bench for the Mavericks to begin the 2022-23 season, Tim Cato of The Athletic reports. Hardaway began last season as a starter for Dallas but took on a bench role in December and January prior to sustaining a fractured foot that forced him to miss the second half of the year. The 30-year-old's role remained relatively steady after he shifted to the bench, so he should still have a chance to carve out a fantasy role if he ultimately plays a depth role early this season. Hardaway has been mentioned in some trade discussions during the offseason, but the Mavericks have also indicated that they're excited to get him back following his lengthy absence to close out last season. He's progressed in his recovery from his foot injury during the offseason, but it's not yet clear when he'll ultimately be deemed fully healthy.

Dallas looking to move on?. Dallas has reportedly "explored the trade market" on Hardaway, per Orenzo Almanza of Sports Illustrated. Quoting Cleveland reporter Jake Fisher, Hardaway is "definitely a name they brought to other teams, but he hasn't played in a year and they still got a lot of money left on that deal." Coming off a fractured foot, Hardaway has three years and $54 million remaining on his contract. He averaged 14.2 points per game on 39.4 percent shooting across 42 games last season.

Unlikely to play until November. Nets head coach Steve Nash said Wednesday that Warren (foot) is unlikely to play until at least November, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports. Warren has appeared in just four games over the past two seasons due to two stress fractures in his left foot. He inked a one-year deal with the Nets this offseason, but he's already off to a rocky start and faces another lengthy absence. When available, Warren can be a potent scorer off the bench for Brooklyn, but it's unclear when exactly he'll be able to contribute.

Being brought along slowly. Warren won't be ready for the start of the regular season as he continues his recovery from foot issues, but coach Steve Nash suggested Wednesday a November return wasn't off the table, Nick Friedell of ESPN reports. The 29-year-old forward has played only four games over the last two seasons due to stress fractures in his left foot, so Brooklyn has no intention of pushing Warren back into action before he's ready. "I think we're going to assess again in November, but he's doing great," Nash said. "He's building up. We knew this was going in. And we also don't want to take big risks with T.J. because he's been out for two years. So it's a process that we want to be very confident in and make a firm organization not to rush him." Once Warren does join the lineup and is back up to full speed, he should have a significant role in the frontcourt and could even fill the starting spot at power forward if Ben Simmons is lined up elsewhere.

Well-rounded line Monday. Harris scored nine points (3-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT) while adding four rebounds, four assists and a steal in 16 minutes during Monday's preseason win over the Nets. That will likely be the 30-year-old's job during the regular season as well, as he rounds out the supporting cast for the Sixers behind superstars Joel Embiid and James Harden, but Harris should still put up solid fantasy numbers in that role.

Perfect from the field. Jones scored 11 points (2-2 FG, 1-1 3 Pt, 2-2 FT) with five rebounds, four assists and a steal in 21 minutes against the Magic on Thursday. The Spurs couldn't have asked for much more out of Jones as the point guard came out with three quick assists in the first quarter, all of which set up three-point field goals for San Antonio. He also grabbed two rebounds and a steal in the quarter, while going 2-of-2 from the field. Jones added another assist for three in the third quarter to go along with three rebounds while remaining perfect from the field. The Spurs have to feel good about Jones' efficiency across the board as they head into the regular season.

Could assume starting role. Jones is one of the top candidates to replace Dejounte Murray as the Spurs' starting point guard, Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reports. A second-round pick in the 2020 draft, Jones has spent the last two years gaining experience on the bench, but with Murray now in Atlanta, the 22-year-old will be asked to take on a much bigger role in the backcourt. During a five-game stretch in the starting five at the end of last season, Jones averaged 14.0 points, 8.2 assists and 4.6 rebounds per game. Joshua Primo, a lottery pick in 2021, appears to be his primary competition for the starting spot.

Drops 22 points Thursday. Young compiled 22 points (8-19 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 6-8 FT), two rebounds and three assists in 30 minutes in a 123-113 win Thursday in a preseason game against Milwaukee in Abu Dhabi. Young played all 12 minutes in both the first and third quarters in his first preseason game. After a 3-for-10 start from the field, he made five of his last nine shots. Young and Dejounte Murray combined for 47 points in their first game as teammates, each finding time to run the offense. The 24-year-old has combined to average 27.8 points and 9.5 assists over the last three seasons, making two All-Star teams.

Has lofty goals. Young is eager for Atlanta's ceiling with the offseason acquisition of Dejounte Murray, via Pat Benson of Sports Illustrated. Young added, "this year, I'm just so locked in on winning a championship and nothing else." He averaged a dominant 28.4 points, 9.7 assists and 3.7 rebounds across 76 games in 2021-22, but he could be due for a volume regression playing alongside Murray. The duo's dynamic is a situation to monitor early in the season.

Resting Tuesday. The Heat announced that Oladipo will miss Tuesday's preseason game versus the Timberwolves due to rest. Inks four-year extension with Miami. Herro and the Heat agreed to terms Sunday on a four-year, $130 million contract extension, Adrian Wojnarowski of ESPN reports. The 13th overall pick in 2019 has been a key piece for Miami over the last three seasons, which he he capped off with a Sixth Man of the Year campaign in 2021-22. Herro appeared in 66 contests last season, averaging 20.7 points, 5.0 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 2.7 made threes in 32.6 minutes per game. The Heat clearly view the 22-year-old as a foundational player, and at some point in the future it's very possible that he could move into a starting role. However, with Miami returning most of last year's roster, Herro will likely find himself in a similar position this season.

In dark on extension. Herro isn't sure if there's been any progress toward a contract extension between his agent and the Heat, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports. "I mean, I know as much as you know," Herro said Tuesday. "I'm just waiting on my turn and we'll see what happens. There's a deadline, but I'm going to let my agent take care of that and see what happens." The guard also shrugged off trade rumors that have seen him linked to nearly every big-name player said to be available around the league. "I mean ever since I've been here, my name has been in rumors. So rumors, they don't bother me. Whether I'm on the Heat or somewhere else, I'm getting ready for the season." Miami has seemed interested in making a splash in the trade market, whether for Kevin Durant, Donovan Mitchell or someone else. Herro would almost certainly be a big part of any package headed the other way. A contract extension would make him far more difficult to ship out until next offseason, though, so Herro may have to wait until the front office determines no deal is feasible before he sees any movement toward an extension.

Dealing with back tightness. Barton didn't play in Friday's preseason opener against the Warriors in Japan due to lower-back tightness, Ava Wallace of The Washington Post reports. The 31-year-old apparently had his back tighten up during the long flight to Japan, so the Wizards opted to play it safe and hold him out of Friday's exhibition, per Wallace. It appears to be a minor concern since coach Wes Unseld Jr. said Barton would have played were it the regular season.

Projected to start. Barton is expected to be the starting small forward for the Wizards' season opener, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports. With Michael Porter being sidelined almost all of last season with a back injury, Barton did an exceptional job filling his role on the Nuggets, averaging 14.7 points and 4.8 rebounds per night. The 31-year-old is an underrated three-level scorer who can also defend multiple positions with his size and length. Expect Barton to provide some offensive firepower as the Wizards' starting small forward.

Double-double in win. Hernangomez produced 11 points (5-8 FG, 1-1 FT), 11 rebounds and an assist in 13 minutes in a 111-98 win Sunday in San Antonio.
